source.title_on_document: No Evidence for LLMs Being Useful in Problem Reframing

supplement.where: The document mentions no supplementary material, online appendix, or data or code repository. Appendices A-E (LLM prompts and interfaces, quiz, design problems, pilot study, demographics) are inside this PDF, pp. 17-25. Footnote 1 (p. 1) links an interactive demo: https://joongishin.github.io/problemReframing_llm/.
supplement.holds: Nothing statistical beyond the main text. No table of arm means, SDs, or test statistics for novelty or usefulness appears anywhere in the document. The main results are box plots (Figure 5, p. 8) and 'all p > 0.05' (pp. 8-9, Section 5.2).

paper_design_summary: Designers recruited on Prolific and CloudResearch were randomly assigned to reframe one of three design problems without an LLM (MANUAL) or with GPT-4o in one of three ways: DIRECT (button-generated frames), STRUCTURED (a button-driven prompt chain through Dorst's nine steps), or FREE-FORM (chat in the default ChatGPT on the participant's own account). Of 456 recruited and assigned, 280 were analyzed, and each wrote two problem frames and picked the best one. Fifteen high-quiz-score participants, blind to condition, rated those 280 frames for novelty and usefulness, while agency, ownership, perceived helpfulness (CSI), and effort (NASA-TLX) were self-reported.

studies.label: Main online experiment (problem reframing, four conditions)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Reframing approach (MANUAL without an LLM, or DIRECT, STRUCTURED, FREE-FORM with GPT-4o) and one of three design problems (aging, misbehavior, preference conflict)
assignment.quote: Our study followed a between-subjects design with four levels: (manual, direct, free-form, and structured). Participants were assigned to these conditions in line with balanced Latin square randomization.
assignment.locator: p. 5, Section 4.1; also p. 5, Section 4 ('We randomly assigned participants to one of the conditions'), p. 6, Figure 4 caption ('Each was randomly assigned an approach'), and p. 7, Section 4.5 ('randomly assigned a reframing approach and problem')

arms.name: MANUAL
arms.description: Baseline: designers reframe the problem by themselves, without an LLM.

arms.name: DIRECT
arms.description: Designers press a 'Reframe' button that sends fixed prompts to GPT-4o to (re)generate alternative problem frames from the problem description, then build on or submit them. AI role: ideas_supplied.

arms.name: STRUCTURED
arms.description: Button-driven GPT-4o prompt chain through Dorst's nine-step reframing process. It shows intermediate content (apparent problems, stakeholders, themes) and final frames. Users can regenerate content per step or add their own. AI role: ideas_supplied.

arms.name: FREE-FORM
arms.description: Designers converse freely with the default ChatGPT (GPT-4o) on their own account and submit the conversation log. AI role: open_chat.

participants.exclusions: 456 were recruited, and Figure 4 shows all 456 randomized and submitting frames. 176 people (456 minus 280, a number the paper does not print) were removed after assignment: people who failed attention-check questions, submitted frames in incorrect format, or spent less than 10 minutes on the reframing task, plus people assigned to an LLM approach who did not use the LLM. The last rule applies only to the LLM arms. Per-reason and per-arm exclusion counts are not reported, so differential attrition cannot be checked. The analysis keeps only the 280 who passed these filters, so it is not intention-to-treat. Analyzed: MANUAL 62, DIRECT 72, STRUCTURED 88, FREE-FORM 58 (LLM arms 218).
participants.who: People with a design background (product, UI/UX, graphic, and game design, architecture, fashion) screened on Prolific and CloudResearch. 76% had more than three years of design experience, all but five had reframed problems in design projects, and 56% had used AI in design tasks. The 280 analyzed were 145 women, 128 men, and 7 other. Paid 16 euros, with a 5-euro bonus for the top 10% of frames.
participants.quote: We recruited 456 individuals by means of the two crowdsourcing platforms. ... We also removed people who were assigned to LLM-based approaches but did not use LLMs. In the end, we had 280 participants
participants.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2 and Figure 4; per-arm counts p. 9, Figure 8 (table on right); demographics p. 25, Table 10; bonus p. 7, Section 4.5

ai_tool.name_model: OpenAI GPT-4o (August 2024); FREE-FORM used the default ChatGPT (GPT-4o) on participants' own accounts
ai_tool.how_used: Roles differ by arm, so no single code describes the study and the field is coded other. FREE-FORM is open_chat: free chat with the default ChatGPT (GPT-4o) on the participant's own account, with the conversation log submitted. DIRECT is ideas_supplied: a 'Reframe' button sends GPT-4o one of two fixed prompts (one for the first frames, one asking for different frames) and returns problem frames. STRUCTURED is ideas_supplied: buttons run a fixed nine-step prompt chain that returns intermediate content and frames, and users can regenerate content within a step or add their own. In the LLM arms participants could submit LLM frames directly or build on them, and they explained how each frame helps solve the problem. Each contrast takes the role of its AI arm: FREE-FORM vs MANUAL is open_chat, DIRECT vs MANUAL and STRUCTURED vs MANUAL are ideas_supplied, and LLM-ALL vs MANUAL pools both roles. Codebook section 8, rule 3 points the primary ai_vs_bau record to FREE-FORM vs MANUAL. That rule picks an arm for the primary record and does not set this field.

task.description: Reframe one of three written design problems (aging delivery drivers, cigarette-butt littering, conflicting office lunch preferences) into the two alternative problem frames the participant found most novel and useful, written in Dorst's template ('If the problem of {initial problem} is approached as if {alternative perspective}, then the direction of solutions could be {potential solutions}'), with an explanation of how each frame helps. In the post-survey the participant picked the frame they liked most. Only that frame was rated.
task.duration: Paid for 'their hour of effort' (p. 6). Mean time to create two frames: 23.25 min (SD 14.73) MANUAL, 21.82 (SD 11.95) DIRECT, 28.35 (SD 18.00) STRUCTURED, 20.78 (SD 9.34) FREE-FORM (p. 8, Section 5).

outcomes.name: Novelty of the problem frame (expert rated)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Fifteen raters drawn from the study's own participants who answered at least three of the five quiz items correctly (Table 11, p. 25), blind to condition (p. 5, Section 4.1). Questionnaires adopted from Doshi and Hauser [21] asked how novel a perspective each frame introduces compared with the original problem description (p. 7, Section 4.4). Each rater reviewed 36 frames randomly sampled across 4 approaches x 3 problems x 3 frames (p. 6, Section 4.3). Figure 5 plots scores on a 1-9 axis. The scale, the number of raters per frame, and how ratings were combined per frame are not stated. Tests named in the method: Mann-Whitney U (MANUAL vs LLM-ALL) and Kruskal-Wallis (four approaches), with Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction as the post hoc procedure (p. 8, Section 5). No pair-specific post hoc result is printed (pp. 8-9, Section 5.2).

arms.name: MANUAL

In S1 this arm reframes without an LLM. The per-approach total is not printed (3 x 3 = 9 by arithmetic).

arms.description: Listed by inference, as for MANUAL. Appendix D does not describe the interface or model. In S1 this arm builds on button-generated GPT-4o frames. The per-approach total is not printed (3 x 3 = 9 by arithmetic).

arms.name: STRUCTURED
arms.description: Listed by inference, as for MANUAL. Appendix D does not describe the interface or model. In S1 this arm uses a nine-step GPT-4o prompt chain. The per-approach total is not printed (3 x 3 = 9 by arithmetic).

arms.name: FREE-FORM
arms.description: Listed by inference, as for MANUAL. Appendix D does not describe the interface or model. In S1 this arm chats with the default ChatGPT. The per-approach total is not printed (3 x 3 = 9 by arithmetic).

participants.who: People from design-related industries, recruited with the same procedure and platforms as the main study; 17 women and 19 men
participants.quote: Using the same procedure and platforms as for the main study, we recruited 36 people

ai_tool.name_model: Not stated for the pilot. Appendix D names no model. The main study used GPT-4o (p. 2, Section 1), and Section 6.4 says 'the tests used only GPT-4o' (p. 13) without saying whether this covers the pilot.
ai_tool.how_used: Appendix D does not describe the pilot's tools. It says only that the pilot used 'the same procedure and platforms as for the main study' and assigned three people to 'each design problem and approach', with 12 per problem, which gives four approaches. It names no approach, interface, or model. If the pilot used the S1 approaches, roles were mixed as in S1 (open_chat in FREE-FORM, ideas_supplied in DIRECT and STRUCTURED), so the field is coded other.

task.description: Same problem-reframing task on the three design problems, used to check that the problems can be reframed into both low- and high-quality frames.

company_involvement.description: No company role is stated. The authors are at Aalto University. Funding came from the Research Council of Finland (357578), the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence (328400, 345604, 341763), a European Research Council Advanced Grant (101141916), and two Aalto University departments. GPT-4o and ChatGPT were used as tools, and FREE-FORM participants used their own ChatGPT accounts.
company_involvement.locator: p. 14, Acknowledgments; p. 1, author affiliations; p. 7, Section 4.5

eligibility.reason: S1 meets all three criteria. It randomly assigned individuals (balanced Latin square randomization, p. 5, Section 4.1) to a no-LLM MANUAL arm or one of three GPT-4o arms. It analyzed 280 people (MANUAL 62, DIRECT 72, STRUCTURED 88, FREE-FORM 58; p. 9, Figure 8), far above 50. Raters blind to condition scored the novelty and usefulness of each participant's chosen frame, written with the assigned approach (p. 6, Section 4.3; p. 7, Section 4.4; p. 8, Figure 5). Caveats: 176 of 456 were dropped after assignment, including LLM-arm participants who did not use the LLM, a rule with no counterpart in MANUAL, and per-arm attrition is not reported. The raters were themselves study participants. The pilot S2 (36 people randomized) is below 50 and reports no comparison by condition. The challenge round changed the AI-role code and the wording of the pairwise results. Neither touches a criterion.

one_line_finding: Of 456 designers randomized to reframe a design problem without an LLM or with GPT-4o in three ways, 280 were analyzed, and rater-scored novelty and usefulness of the frame each person picked as best did not differ between MANUAL (62 analyzed) and LLM-ALL (218 analyzed) or among the four approaches (all p > 0.05), reported only as box plots (p. 6, Figure 4 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Figure 5; pp. 8-9, Section 5.2).
open_questions: No arm means, SDs, or test statistics for novelty or usefulness are printed. Extraction needs data from the authors or figure digitizing. Figure 5 shows box plots, which usually mark medians and quartiles rather than means, and the paper does not define their elements.
Per-arm randomized counts and per-arm exclusion counts are not reported. The exclusion of LLM-arm non-users applies only to the AI arms, so attrition may differ by arm.

The rating scale, the number of raters per frame, and how ratings were combined are not stated. 15 raters x 36 frames = 540 ratings over 280 frames would be about two per frame, but the paper does not say so.

The AI role differs by arm: FREE-FORM is open chat, while DIRECT and STRUCTURED supply LLM-generated frames. The study-level field is coded other, and how_used gives each arm's and each contrast's role. Review 1 may prefer a role per arm or per contrast in the form.
Whether problem reframing counts as idea_generation or as 'other' task type.

The raters were phase-1 participants with high quiz scores, recruited from the same crowdsourcing pool, who rated other participants' frames. The paper does not say whether they came from the 280 analyzed or the 456 recruited.
S2 (pilot): Appendix D names no approach, interface, or model. Four approaches follow from three people per problem-and-approach cell and 12 per problem.

The paper names Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction as its post hoc procedure but prints no pair-specific result for novelty or usefulness, and it does not say whether it ran pairwise tests after the Kruskal-Wallis tests. The FREE-FORM vs MANUAL record that codebook section 8, rule 3 makes primary therefore has no pair-specific statistic.
Version: the file is arXiv v1 of 3 March 2025, typeset as the CHI '25 paper. The ACM Digital Library version of record was not compared, and retrieval.json has no version_saved note.
notes: Outcomes not listed because they are self-reported, not scored on the output: perceived agency and ownership (no significant MANUAL vs LLM-ALL or across-approach differences, all p > 0.05; p. 8, Figure 6; p. 9, Section 5.3), the Creativity Support Index for the LLM arms only (DIRECT 64.28, SD 18.90; STRUCTURED 64.85, SD 20.00; FREE-FORM 61.01, SD 17.19; no significant differences; p. 10, Section 5.4; p. 9, Figure 7), and NASA-TLX effort (no significant differences; p. 9, Figure 7; p. 10, Section 5.4). Time to create frames is reported by arm (p. 8, Section 5) but is not a creativity outcome. The expertise analysis (H4) is not coded as a contrast, because expertise was measured by the quiz rather than assigned and both groups compared used an LLM. Within the LLM arms, quiz 'experts' (3+ correct; 79 of the 280 analyzed, 61 in the LLM arms; p. 9, Figure 8) produced frames rated 12.54% more novel than novices (Z = 2.70, p = 0.01). The FREE-FORM gap of 20.84% was not significant (Z = 2.31, p = 0.06), and usefulness showed no differences (all p > 0.05) (pp. 11-12, Section 5.5; p. 11, Figure 10). Experts also reported more agency in LLM-ALL (Z = 2.05, p = 0.04) and in STRUCTURED (Z = 2.29, p = 0.02, 15.69% more) (p. 12, Section 5.5). The expertise split was balanced across arms, chi2(3, N = 280) = 0.70, p = 0.87 (p. 11). No diversity or similarity outcome is reported. Power analysis (G*Power): 220 and 280 participants needed to detect medium effects at 95% power (p. 8, Section 5.1). S2 (pilot, p. 25, Appendix D): the authors internally reviewed frame quality and found 2-3 of 12 frames per problem novel or useful. No comparison by condition is reported, so S2 lists no outcomes. Reconciler addition: the DIRECT vs FREE-FORM ai_design contrast, which neither screener listed, rests on the same blanket statement ('among all the individual approaches (all p > 0.05)'), and no pair-specific test is printed. The search-record note 'N=280 with no unit stated' is confirmed as 280 people (p. 6, Section 4.2). Finalized 2026-10-05: the three challenge problems (two from the assignment lens and one from the outcome lens, while the people lens found none) were checked against the PDF, and all three corrections were applied. Spec alignment: arm counts in contrasts and in one_line_finding now say 'analyzed', participants.exclusions says that 176 is 456 minus 280 and that the analysis is not intention-to-treat, and participants.who ties the gender counts to the 280 analyzed. The reconciliation object is unchanged, so it keeps three statements the final form corrects: the open_chat role for S1 and S2, 'the paper's post hoc Dunn's tests compare pairs of approaches', and 'Its post hoc tests compare pairs, and every pair gave p > 0.05'.

open_items.item: Statistics (open question 1): no arm means, SDs, or test statistics for novelty or usefulness are printed, only the Figure 5 box plots and 'all p > 0.05'. The paper names no supplement or data repository. Effect sizes need arm-level data from the authors, or figure digitizing as a fallback.

Attrition by arm (open question 2): per-arm counts at assignment and per-arm exclusions are not printed, and only the LLM arms had a no-use filter. Random assignment is stated and 280 were analyzed, so criteria 1 and 2 hold either way. The gap bears on risk of bias, not eligibility.

Rating procedure (open question 3): the scale, the number of raters per frame, and how ratings were combined are not stated. Raters blind to condition scored each analyzed frame, so criterion 3 holds either way.

AI role (open question 4): the study-level role is now other, and how_used gives open_chat for FREE-FORM and ideas_supplied for DIRECT and STRUCTURED. The source is clear, and the choice of a study-level code is for Review 1.

Task type (open question 5): idea_generation or other for problem reframing. Either way the task asks for frames with more than one acceptable answer, judged on novelty and usefulness, so it is a creative or ideation task under codebook section 1.

Raters (open question 6): the 15 raters were participants with three or more quiz items correct who rated other participants' frames, blind to condition. The paper does not say whether they came from the 280 analyzed or the 456 recruited. Review 1 may prefer human_raters to expert_raters for them. Criterion 3 holds under either code.
Pilot tools (open question 7): Appendix D names no approach, interface, or model for S2. S2 has 36 people and no comparison by condition, so it enters no estimate.

Pairwise tests (open question 8): no pair-specific post hoc result is printed, so the FREE-FORM vs MANUAL record that rule 3 makes primary, and every other single-arm contrast, rests on the blanket 'all p > 0.05' and Figure 5. Pair-level statistics need the authors' data.
Version (open question 9): the file is arXiv v1 of 3 March 2025, typeset as the CHI '25 paper with its DOI. The ACM version of record was not compared.
